tools.description_en: Create a parametric Part::Box solid in FreeCAD (native Python via subprocess FreeCADCmd, no COM, no mouse/pixel actuation) and save it as a .FCStd document. Use for rectangular/cuboid solids when working with FreeCAD instead of AutoCAD.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description_en: Box length (X dimension) in model units.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description_en: Box width (Y dimension) in model units.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description_en: Box height (Z dimension) in model units.

tools.description_en: Create a parametric Part::Cylinder solid in FreeCAD (native Python via subprocess FreeCADCmd, no COM) and save it as a .FCStd document.

Extrude a closed 2D polyline profile into a solid Part::Feature in FreeCAD (native Python via subprocess FreeCADCmd, no COM) and save it as a .FCStd document. Requires at least 3 [x, y] profile points; auto-closes the profile if the first and last points differ.

parameters.name: points_list
parameters.description_en: List of at least 3 [x, y] points forming the profile to extrude.

tools.description_en: Open an EXISTING .FCStd document, run a modification script against it (bound to the local name 'doc'), and save back to the SAME path. This is the preferred 'Modify Existing' revision path for iterative CAD design — use this instead of create_freecad_box/create_freecad_cylinder/create_freecad_extrusion once a project file already exists, so edits (a new boolean cut, a changed parameter, an added feature) accumulate in one evolving document instead of scattering a new .FCStd per operation.

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description_en: Absolute path to the existing .FCStd document to open and modify.

parameters.name: modification_script
parameters.description_en: Python source that edits the already-opened document (available as 'doc'), e.g. adding a Part::Cylinder and a Part::Cut against an existing object, or changing an existing object's parameter.

_intent: add a cut to the existing box

tools.description_en: Run an arbitrary Python script inside FreeCAD via subprocess FreeCADCmd (the FreeCAD/Part/Sketcher APIs are available) — for geometry or operations the create_freecad_* primitives don't cover. Unlike those, success is judged only by the subprocess exit code (no marker check), since the script defines its own notion of success. Prefer create_freecad_box/create_freecad_cylinder/create_freecad_extrusion when they cover the need.

parameters.name: python_script_str
parameters.description_en: Full Python source to execute inside FreeCADCmd's bundled interpreter.

tools.description_en: Assembles previously-generated CAD parts (.stl mesh artifacts from create_freecad_*/export operations) into a single kinematic URDF (Unified Robot Description Format) robot model — the universal interchange hub for ROS2, Gazebo, and Isaac Sim. Each part becomes a URDF link (optionally carrying its mesh as visual+collision geometry); each connection between two links becomes a URDF joint (fixed, revolute, or continuous). Saves '<robot_name>.urdf' to the workspace.

parameters.name: robot_name
parameters.description_en: Name of the robot assembly; also used as the output filename (<robot_name>.urdf).

parameters.name: links
parameters.description_en: Ordered list of link objects, each: {"name": str, "mesh_path": optional str — a previously-generated .stl artifact path or filename to attach as this link's visual+collision geometry; omit for a purely kinematic frame with no geometry, "origin_xyz": optional [x, y, z] offset applied to the mesh geometry}.

parameters.name: joints
parameters.description_en: Ordered list of joint objects connecting two links, each: {"name": optional str, "parent": str link name, "child": str link name, "type": "fixed"|"revolute"|"continuous", "origin_xyz": optional [x, y, z] — the child frame's offset from the parent, "axis": optional [x, y, z] — the rotation axis for revolute/continuous joints, defaults to [0, 0, 1]}.

_intent: assemble a robot from these parts
